newsitem.title: USA: Micron shares off with DRAM prices falling.
newsitem.headline: Micron shares off with DRAM prices falling.

text.p: Micron Technology Inc shares fell amid evidence of a further decline in prices of DRAM memory chips, its main product.
Micron was off 1-1/4 to 22-3/8 at midday in activity that included a large block trade, market sources said.

Semiconductor analyst Charles Boucher of UBS Securities said prices of four-megabyte DRAMs, the most commonly used memory chip in personal computers, have fallen in recent days to $1.90 in several Asian markets. In Japan they are selling for $2.00. Two weeks ago, four-megabyte DRAMs cost about $2.50, he said.
Boucher said it was not clear if the decline in DRAM prices was the reason Micron's stock was lower.
Prices for memory chips have fallen since the winter and Micron Technology shares have dropped in tandem with them, from a 52-week high of 94-1/2 to as low as 16-5/8.
Micron was trading down 1-1/4 at 22-3/8 Monday afternoon.
Analysts previously said DRAM prices of $2.50 were close to being less than the variable cost of making them.
Micron and other memory chip makers have been converting their production lines to manufacture 16-megabyte DRAMs, which are being installed in newer PCs.
However, prices for 16-megabyte DRAMS have also fallen to about $9 to $10 currently from about $11 to $12 two weeks ago. They had dropped to as low as $8 on the spot market.
"The rate of decline is slowing but prices are still trending downward," Boucher said.

Still, the analyst said he could not directly link the latest round of price cuts to the decline in Micron's stock on Monday. He said some traders and investors might be surprised to learn DRAM prices were still falling, while others who follow the topic closely would not be surprised.

Bear Stearns analyst Nimal Vallipuram also said "there is nothing specific" to account for Micron's decline Monday, though further erosion of DRAM prices was a worry for everyone in the business, he added.
